body:
Second CUDA data point, on a different quantisation and OS, plus a width structure that may narrow this.

RTX 3090 (sm_86), driver 610.43.02, Debian 13, built from `c060ca9` with CUDA 13.3. Target is `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF` `UD-Q4_K_XL` rather than your IQ2_M and KV is `q8_0` rather than `q4_0`, so this is a different point in the same space. `-c 8192 -fa on --parallel 1`, greedy, `cache_prompt: false`, 400 tokens, 25 prompts, 5 passes, fresh server per arm per pass. The `draft-dflash` arms are PR #27342 at `d1a522f` and are compared only against a no-speculation baseline built from that same branch.

The divergence reproduces and is deterministic, as you found. 76 to 80 % of requests differ from their baseline depending on the arm, forking at a median 23 % into the text, and every arm is byte-identical to itself across all five passes.

What might be worth following is that the fork position is a function of verification width. Running `n_max` 2, 3, 4, 5 and 7, so widths 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8, the character index of the first difference is **identical inside two groups and different between them**: widths 3 and 4 agree on 25 of 25 prompts, widths 5, 6 and 8 agree on 25 of 25, and the two groups land somewhere different on 14 of them. Same structure in all five passes. The grouping crosses drafter types, so `draft-mtp` at width 6 sits with `draft-dflash` at widths 5 and 8 rather than with the other `draft-mtp` arms.

It is not monotone either. One prompt diverges at widths 3 and 4 and is byte-identical to baseline at 5, 6 and 8.

`ggml/src/ggml-cuda/mmvq.cu` changes at that width. `ggml_cuda_should_use_mmvq` returns `ne11 <= MMVQ_MAX_BATCH_SIZE`, which is 8 on this fallthrough, so widths 3 through 8 all stay inside MMVQ and the kernel family is not what moves. `calc_nwarps` does move: sm_86 is not RDNA, GCN, CDNA or DGX Spark and the Turing table is gated below AMPERE, so it lands on `MMVQ_PARAMETERS_GENERIC`, which gives 4 warps for `ncols_dst` 1 to 4, 2 warps for 5 to 8, and 1 above that. The warp count feeds `blocks_per_iter`, so each thread walks a different subset of K, and it sets how many partial sums are folded out of `tmp_shared`, so the reduction tree differs too.

That is one boundary coinciding on one architecture at one quantisation, which is consistent with the mechanism and is not proof of it. `n_max` 1 through 8 is running now. That puts widths 2 and 7 in for the first time and adds width 9, where `calc_nwarps` drops to one warp and `should_use_mmvq` stops returning true at the same time. If the grouping tracks the table those come out as {2,3,4}, {5,6,7,8} and {9} on its own; if width 2 or 7 lands in the wrong group it is tracking something else and I will post that.

Three caveats. My KV is `q8_0`, and @snick525 showed in #25618 that q8_0 KV moves greedy output with no speculation on either side; it is held constant across every arm here so it should not produce a width-dependent grouping, but the f16 control is queued rather than run. Your target is IQ2_M and mine is `UD-Q4_K_XL`, so the grouping may not transfer. And I have not run `draft-simple` against this target, so I cannot speak to your result that it stays identical on the coding workload, which is the more interesting half of your table.

The per-prompt fork table and the rest of the setup are in https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/25618#issuecomment-5396293373. Happy to run other controls on this card if any would help.

Hi,
I ran in a similar problem. Did some diging with an AI agent and ended up with some tests, resutts and a fix for my case on an RTX 5090. Here are more informations:

Test Environment:
RTX 5090 (SM120), CUDA 13.3, pilote 610.88
Base tested: f1357e499

Symptom:
Vanilla and MTP being deterministic but diverging in greedy.

Root causes identified:
1) An incorrect MMVF selection order;
2) Different Flash Attention paths and reductions depending on batch width.

Results after fix:
- Exact vanilla ↔ MTP parity for n_max = 1..3;
- divergence still present for n_max >= 4 (not fixed in my branch).

Tests:
- Exact comparisons: 75/75
- Long context: exact
- Flash Attention: 2936/2936
- MUL_MAT: 1193/1193


Branches (The first one is the fix and the other one is where you can find my tests, results and relevants files)
- Fix: https://github.com/Apoze/llama.cpp/tree/fix/cuda-speculative-batch-invariance
- Evidence / reproduction: https://github.com/Apoze/llama.cpp/blob/evidence/cuda-speculative-batch-invariance/evidence/cuda-speculative-batch-invariance


If you want me to create a PR or two, do tell me. Or you can just take what you are interrested in the code right away.
This issue was closed because it has been inactive for 14 days since being marked as stale.
